codeReview.summary: The implementation comprehensively covers all 7 requirements from the feature description: Vite + TypeScript project with COOP/COEP headers, index.html with canvas/controls/debug panel/loading overlay, Emscripten module loader with phase tracking, loading progress UI, Vitest tests (49 total), LZ4 fix (repackaged assets without --lz4), and header verification. Code is well-structured with clean separation between emulator.ts (loader logic), loading.ts (UI state), main.ts (wiring), and style.css (dark theme). TypeScript strict mode clean, all tests pass. The LZ4 fix correctly identifies the root cause (QEMU built without -sLZ4=1) and applies the appropriate solution (remove --lz4 from file_packager). 11 files changed with 1263 insertions.

issues.description: TypeError over-classification in classifyError(): the condition `errName === 'TypeError'` catches ALL TypeErrors as 'network' errors, not just fetch-related ones. A runtime TypeError like `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` would be misclassified as a network error. Should add a more specific message check (e.g., /fetch|network|load/i.test(errMsg)) before the errName fallback, or move the errName check after SharedArrayBuffer.

Misleading comment: `noInitialRun: false` is paired with comment '// Suppress auto-run so we control lifecycle', but `false` means auto-run IS allowed. If the intent is placeholder behavior (Start button wired in later feature), the comment should reflect that. If the intent is truly to suppress auto-run, the value should be `true`.

Double SharedArrayBuffer check: EmulatorLoader.load() checks SAB at line 243, but main.ts also checks SAB at line ~59 before creating the loader. The redundant check in load() is defensive but unnecessary since main.ts already gates on it. Not a bug, just redundant code.

Non-null assertions (`!`) on all DOM element lookups (e.g., `document.getElementById('loading-overlay')!`). If any element ID has a typo or HTML structure changes, this will produce null with no error message, causing confusing runtime failures. Consider adding a guard or assertion with a meaningful error message.

Broad OOM classification: `/memory/i.test(errMsg)` would match any error mentioning 'memory' (e.g., 'Invalid memory address'), not just OOM. The RangeError instanceof check is sufficient for the primary OOM case; the message regex could be more specific (e.g., /out of memory|could not allocate/i).

summary: PASS. The frontend-skeleton feature is well-implemented, covering all required functionality: Emscripten module loader with 6 initialization phases, error classification for 7 error types with user-friendly messages, loading UI with progress bar and smooth transitions, complete HTML structure with canvas/controls/debug panel, dark theme CSS with fullscreen support, and the critical LZ4 fix. 49 tests pass, TypeScript is clean, COOP/COEP headers verified. Five non-blocking issues identified: TypeError over-classification in error handling, misleading noInitialRun comment, redundant SAB check, non-null assertions without fallbacks, and broad OOM regex matching. None are blocking for the skeleton feature — they are refinements for later hardening.
